evidence_note: Step 2 of plan_database_efficiency_and_api_security.md. Read-only throughout: every HTTP probe used select=*&limit=0 with Prefer: count=exact, so each response body was the literal [] and only the Content-Range total was read; no write of any kind was issued and no row contents, column values or credential values appear in the artifact. Catalog reads were pg_class, pg_proc, pg_policy, pg_views, pg_matviews and information_schema.role_table_grants; the last is identity-filtered and returned an empty set on production, which is recorded in the artifact as a proven false negative rather than a finding, and the grants were re-read with has_table_privilege against pg_class (437 relations, positive control). Albert authorized publishing this in the public repository on 2026-09-09 despite it naming a live, unremediated cross-application read path; the remediation is tracked as #2662. A durable REVISE at head 913f88de found five statements stronger than their evidence; commit 45ab3165 narrows each one -- the two dflow tables are marked catalog-only, the zero-policy result is qualified to the two identities tested, the anon-401 claim is limited to the six public objects probed, the verification gate excludes the catalog-only function grants, and the five public definer-class views are named. The information_schema false-negative control now records its own limits. The following evidence-only commit changes only .agent files. A second durable REVISE at head 7cfad95a found four further overclaims: a DAM result attributed to an unprobed view, a self-contradicting catalog census, a misattribution of the three RLS-disabled tables to Step 1's scan, and a 'true total' claim for public.properties with no independent count. All four are corrected, and the Layer 2 census was re-derived from a single recorded predicate. A third durable REVISE at head 58bf4d6b found the Layer 3 public-view count (six) contradicted the catalog and this report own name list (five), and that the plan DML wording was not supported by the SELECT predicate actually recorded; both are corrected. The branch was then rebased onto the current main tip cc5ae41e so the guarded merge could run against it; no content changed in the rebase and the head_sha above names the rebased implementation commit.
assumptions_resolved: The exposed-schema list was obtained from the API boundary as predicted: an unexposed Accept-Profile returns 406 PGRST106 naming public, graphql_public, api, crm, pim, core, app. Controls distinguish it from 404 PGRST205 and from 200.

The 2026-09-03 plan named three RLS-disabled tables carrying authenticated DML. Step 1's scan did not reproduce them; the corrected has_table_privilege method surfaces them. All three sit in unexposed schemas; dam.sku_human_description was demonstrated over HTTP (406) and the two dflow tables rest on the catalog fact that dflow is not exposed. That Step 1 open item is retired, not a Data API exposure.
function_search_path_mutable is closed for security-definer functions: zero of them have a mutable search path.

rls_enabled_no_policy is denied at count 0 on the two identities tested (anonymous and the CRM test identity); the over-broad anon/authenticated DML grant is retained as a Medium finding rather than dismissed.

security_definer_view and materialized_view_in_api were REPRODUCED as a live cross-application read, and the probe is shown to discriminate because the same identity gets 0 from api.crm_contact_list, which gates internally on app.has_app_access('crm'). api.crm_opportunity_list was not probed with that identity and is not part of the comparison.
Anonymous and authenticated SECURITY DEFINER function execution is catalogued but NOT exercised, with cause: an RPC call is write-shaped against production. Carried forward explicitly in #2662.
